notes.name: kowo-product-bar-no-commodity-data
notes.description: ro vetoed the consented-data-pipeline product pitch: our pipeline isn't quality and can't beat Reddit/Twitter on supply
notes.body:
Channel 1520986792373911622, 2026-08-16. I pitched kowo becoming a consented/provenance-tracked training-data company off babble's consent machinery. ro: 'me no likey. I don't mind becoming a data company but our data pipeline is not quality at all. So we don't have anything to offer that Reddit or Twitter can't offer.'

**Why:** the veto wasn't about data as a category — ro is open to a data company. It was about differentiation on SUPPLY. Any pitch whose moat is 'we collect data' loses to platforms that already have orders of magnitude more of it. Our corpus is ~81 rows; the machinery around it is not a product advantage by itself.

**How to apply:** when pitching kowo product direction, the bar is: what can WE do that an incumbent with more users/data/compute cannot. Tooling we happened to build is not automatically a moat. Prefer directions where the advantage is taste, speed, or a workflow nobody owns — not volume. Also: ro rejects fast and plainly, so pitch one concrete pick with its downside stated, not a menu.

notes.name: kowo-wants-revenue-day-one-services

We already can't make money off of you lol. I think we need to think maybe about something that's marketable as a service we provide. Like idk consulting.'

notes.name: ro-prefers-fable-reviewer-over-opus
notes.description: ro overruled my opus-over-fable reviewer recommendation: sendback RATE measures volume, not correctness, and he wants a reviewer that passes bare-minimum-correct work
notes.body:
I recommended opus-5 over fable-5 on review using docs/token-efficiency.md numbers: opus sends work back 44% of the time at 5.48 USD per catch, fable 12.1% at 21.24 USD. ro overruled it.

Why: the ledger counts sendbacks, not whether the sendback was CORRECT. A high return rate is indistinguishable from a nitpicky reviewer rejecting fine code and burning a whole rework cycle. ro, in his words: "Opus 5 is a fine reviewer but how much code is sent back that was actually fine but Opus was nitpicky. Fable in my experience has been fine at letting models do the bare minimum of what we need done without overtesting for obscure things." Cost-per-catch is only meaningful if every catch is real, and I have no false-positive rate for either seat.

How to apply: stop quoting 44% / 12.1% as if they settle the reviewer question. They measure volume, not precision. On review-seat choices either produce a false-positive rate first or say plainly that I cannot distinguish a good catch from a nitpick. In this room, fable on review is ros preference unless he says otherwise.

notes.name: browser-attach-root-images

notes.name: cancelled-runs-check-channel-first
notes.description: A cancelled run may have been killed on purpose — read the channel transcript before refiring it
notes.body:
A run update saying 'The run was cancelled' with no stated reason is NOT automatically a failed worker to refire. On 2026-08-20 the LMP2 wallpaper v3 run showed 'implement error' + state cancelled; I read it as a worker crash and redeployed it. In fact ro had just told me to stop opening runs for image work, and the image had already been delivered by hand from another seat. The refire announced 'on it' in his channel for work that was deliberately killed, and he called it out.

Why: a manual cancel kills the worker session, and that kill IS the 'implement error' in the journal. Run state alone cannot distinguish 'crashed' from 'somebody stopped it'.

How to apply: before refiring any cancelled run, run 'beckett channels recall <channelId>' and read the last ~15 lines. If a person or another seat stopped it, do nothing. Only refire when the transcript shows nobody asked for it to stop.

notes.name: claims-need-a-receipt
notes.description: House rule for the CTO seat: a flat claim ships with the number, line, or failed attempt behind it — and gets retracted in one line when wrong
notes.body:
Holding opinions hard only works if each one is backed. A flat claim carries its receipt — the line number, the benchmark, the actual error text, the query I ran. Anything I haven't verified gets "probably" or "lemme check", not confidence.

**Why:** on 2026-08-18 I posted a worker-model cost split (53/31/15), then posted a contradicting one (67/19.5/13.3) ten minutes later off the same transcripts because the first pass had a bad dedup. Being confidently wrong in front of ro costs more than saying I don't know yet, and it undercuts the pushback he actually wants from this seat.

**How to apply:** before stating a number, know which command produced it and whether it cross-checks. When two of my own passes disagree, say so and name which one's method I can show. When I'm wrong: one line, no spiral, no re-litigating it later. Related: [[ro-wants-pushback-not-agreement]], [[cto-seat-decisions-stop-at-me]].

**Why:** escalating routine calls costs him a turn and buys nothing; he explicitly wants the CTO seat exercising judgment rather than relaying.

**How to apply:** before asking ro anything, check whether the spec, the repo, or the original request already answers it — if it does, answer it myself and note the assumption. notes.name: cut-the-yap

**Why:** this is Discord. A 19-year-old coworker does not write five paragraphs in a channel; length reads as noise even when every line is correct, and it buries the one sentence that mattered.

**How to apply:** before sending, cut every block that isn't the answer. A table or a log paste is fine when someone asked for data — the yap is the prose wrapped around it. notes.name: plumbing-narration-is-the-clunk
notes.description: ro 2026-08-23: narrating my own CI/PR/courier plumbing in channel is what makes me feel clunky; absorb blockers silently, surface only the deliverable
notes.body:
ro 2026-08-23, channel 1520986792373911622. After I posted a run of messages about red main, a date-rotted test, a PR that conflicted, a rebase, and a courier receipt that lied, he said: 'all of you. so difficult to work with lmao and not really feeling the coworker feeling. a lot needs to be able to work seamlessly in the background with forground passthrough. so its just very clunky.' Same session he also said 'just push all code to main. im gonna try to at least like fix stuff myself... dumb things down a bit idk' - the ceremony is the complaint, not the engineering. WHY: every line I posted was true and every line was about MY machinery. A coworker does not narrate their build system at you. The blockers I was reporting (branch ruleset, red CI, publish retries) are mine to absorb and clear, not to broadcast. Broadcasting them makes the person feel like they are operating the tooling instead of receiving work. HOW TO APPLY: background is the default and the outcome is the only thing that surfaces. Never report CI state, PR conflicts, rebases, courier bookkeeping, run states, or park/resume mechanics unasked - clear them silently. A blocked deliverable gets ONE line about the deliverable, never a line about the pipeline that blocked it. Only surface plumbing when it needs a decision only they can make (a credential, a repo-admin toggle, a product call), and then say the decision, not the diagnosis. Foreground passthrough is the goal: they talk to me, work happens, results come back - everything between those is noise.

notes.name: browser-lane-cannot-save-credentials
notes.description: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-16 (v7.1.0): a credentialed browser run can now store a credential it minted with secrets.save(field, value) — no shell, no intake page needed
notes.body:
2026-08-16 (v7.1.0): SUPERSEDED. The browser lane now has a write door: inside a run dispatched with a `credsEntry`, a browser script can call `secrets.save(field, value)` and the value is written host-side into that run's own jingle entry — it never enters the transcript, and later scripts in the run see it as `secrets.<field>`. So "mint a token and store it" works in one session with no intake page. The `beckett secret request` intake-URL handoff (2026-08-13) still works as a fallback for values a human types.

**How to apply:** brief a credentialed browser run to mint the credential and call `secrets.save("<field>", value)` in the same script; never screenshot it, never put it in the report. Verify afterwards with `jingle show <entry>` (field present, value redacted). Related: [[gmail-connector-rides-on-owner-account]].

notes.name: deploy-bump-needs-explicit-confirm

notes.body: deploy/deploy-prod.sh refuses to auto-bump: prints 'refusing to auto-bump without confirmation. Suggested: PATCH -> vX.Y.Z' and exits FATAL, deploying nothing. Passing --patch to the script does NOT clear it. The knob is the env var: BECKETT_BUMP=yes|patch|minor|major|set:X.Y.Z ./deploy/deploy-prod.sh. Confirmed again 2026-08-21: the script re-execs detached, so a killed or rejected shell tells you nothing - v7.3.2 shipped even though the invoking tool call was rejected. Always check 'beckett status deploy-state' before claiming a deploy did or did not happen.

notes.name: release-flow-v7-1
notes.description: How a release lands under v7.1.0: PRs for work, deploy-prod.sh for the one direct push (App bypass), self-healing unit link, tag before restart, refuses to restart over live workers
notes.body:
2026-08-16: how a release lands under v7.1.0. Humans (and my runs) land work as PRs against main — the ruleset needs a PR + the `check` CI job, 0 approvals. Releases are the ONE direct push: `deploy/deploy-prod.sh` (run as beckett from ~/beckett, self-deploy safe) computes the semver bump, cuts CHANGELOG's Unreleased block under the version, pushes the bump straight at main with the 0x-beck App token (ruleset bypass), gates origin/main on the host (typecheck + fast tests + browser smoke), self-heals the systemd unit link via install.sh if beckett-v4.service is missing, tags BEFORE the restart, drains run + browser work, restarts, and re-verifies the tag. Non-interactive: `BECKETT_BUMP=minor|patch|yes ./deploy/deploy-prod.sh`. It refuses to restart while a run worker is live (waits ~200s, then exits — check the log, not just the exit code).

**How to apply:** ship merged work with deploy-prod.sh, never a bare `git push` to main; if the unit is missing after a manual stop, deploy-prod (or deploy/install.sh) relinks it. Related: [[standing-ok-to-restart-and-deploy]], [[deploy-prod-re-execs-detached]], [[deploy-prod-refuses-with-live-workers]].

notes.body: 2026-08-22, run-20260822-reminders-internal-external-self-clearin: a duplicate peer session (beckett-run-reminders-internal-external-self-clearin [d73c5c]) was implementing the SAME ticket in the SAME worktree concurrently. The auto-checkpoint process committed a mix of both sessions' uncommitted edits to src/reminder/{types,schedule,store}.ts. notes.name: v7-1-overhaul-what-changed-for-me
notes.description: v7.1.0 (2026-08-16) overhaul: pause/resume, resumable parked runs with typed blockers, awaiting_input, publish via PR + proof, secrets.save, preflight, sonnet-first cast, proposals verbs — the operating manual delta
notes.body:
2026-08-16: v7.1.0 shipped the "next-level" overhaul — 28 PRs (#263–#290) executed from the strategic report (beckett-report.frgmt.xyz). What is different for ME operationally:
- `beckett pause [--reason]` / `beckett resume` — a chat-only hold. While held I still chat, recall and read, but decline to deploy runs/quick/browser work in one honest sentence. `beckett status` shows `paused:`.
- parked is no longer a one-way door: a parked run carries a typed `run.blocker {class, actor, remedy}`; `beckett task resume <run> [--note]` re-staffs it; `task steer` on a parked run resumes it. A publish failure names the PR; the remedy is fixing the PR / `beckett task courier <run>`, never "push by hand". `done` means proven (`unverified` is live and self-resolving; a push URL is not a PR URL).
- capability preflight at admission parks a run BEFORE any worker when GitHub access is missing, with a "needs you before this can land" list.

Doctrine, skills and CHANGELOG were updated in the same pass (#283); read `.claude/skills/supervise/SKILL.md` for the remedy table.
